nodes.title: ElastiCache cluster has no AUTH token configured
nodes.description: The ElastiCache Redis cluster 'ecommerce-cache' does not require an AUTH token for client authentication. Any client that can reach port 6379 has unrestricted read/write access to all cached data, including session tokens and JWT blacklist entries.

control.name: ElastiCache Redis clusters should require AUTH tokens
control.description: Enabling AUTH for Redis prevents unauthenticated access to cached data.

securitySubCategories.title: Ensure ElastiCache for Redis clusters use encryption in transit and at rest
6.3 - Ensure all stored data is adequately secured

nodes.title: Security group allows unrestricted inbound access to Redis port 6379
nodes.description: Security group 'ecommerce-cache' (sg-0ec3a92f1d4b78c45) permits inbound TCP traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 6379. Combined with the absence of Redis AUTH, this exposes cached data to any internet-accessible client.

control.name: Security groups should not permit unrestricted access to sensitive ports
control.description: Unrestricted inbound access to database and cache ports increases the attack surface.

securitySubCategories.title: 1.3.1 - Prohibit direct public access to any component in the cardholder data environment

nodes.title: ECS task definition does not specify a non-root user
nodes.description: The ECS task definition 'ecommerce-api:7' runs container processes as root (UID 0). If an application vulnerability allows code execution, the attacker has root-level access to the container filesystem and can potentially escape the container.

control.name: ECS task definitions should specify a non-root user
control.description: Running containers as non-root reduces the blast radius of container compromises.

nodes.title: ECS task definition contains sensitive environment variables in plaintext
nodes.description: The ECS task definition 'ecommerce-api:7' passes sensitive values (DATABASE_URL, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY) as plaintext environment variables. These values are visible in the ECS task definition and CloudTrail logs. Secrets should be referenced from AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store.

control.name: ECS task definitions should use secrets management for sensitive values
control.description: Use secretsFrom or valueFrom referencing Secrets Manager/SSM to avoid exposing secrets in task definitions.

nodes.title: RDS security group allows inbound access from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 5432
nodes.description: Security group 'ecommerce-db' permits inbound TCP traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 5432 (PostgreSQL). This is a developer convenience rule intended for local access but has not been restricted before deployment.

control.name: RDS security groups should restrict inbound access to known CIDRs
control.description: Direct public access to database instances should be avoided. Use VPN or bastion host for administrative access.

securitySubCategories.title: 2.2.1 - Develop configuration standards for all system components

nodes.title: CloudWatch log group has short retention period
nodes.description: CloudWatch log group '/aws/ecs/ecommerce-api' has a retention period of 7 days. Security events and audit logs will be automatically purged, limiting forensic capability and compliance requirements.

control.name: CloudWatch log groups should retain logs for at least 90 days
control.description: Log retention should meet compliance requirements and support incident investigation.

nodes.title: ECS task definition does not set readonlyRootFilesystem
nodes.description: The ECS task definitions 'ecommerce-api:7' and 'ecommerce-client:5' do not set readonlyRootFilesystem to true. A writable root filesystem increases the risk of persistent compromise if a container is breached.

control.name: ECS containers should use a read-only root filesystem
control.description: A read-only root filesystem prevents malware from writing persistent files after a container is compromised.

securitySubCategories.title: 5.12 - Ensure the container's root filesystem is mounted as read only
